defects: Conclusion uses DenseRange of a map into the plain product type (ι → F) instead of Π i, WithAbs (v i); it never invokes WithAbs, so the codomain does not carry the topology induced by each v i — the density claim is disconnected from the absolute values and is either vacuous/discrete or differently-typed than intended.

Pairwise hypothesis is stated as mere function inequality (v i ≠ v j) rather than topological inequivalence (¬(v i).IsEquiv (v j)); this is strictly weaker — two distinct absolute values can still be equivalent (e.g. v and v^c), so the produced hypothesis admits counterexamples where the density conclusion actually fails, making the produced theorem false as stated.
Uses [Fintype ι] instead of [Finite ι], a strictly stronger (data-bearing) finiteness assumption rather than the Prop-valued finiteness in the gold statement.

Nontriviality hypothesis is spelled out as ∃ x ≠ 0, v i x ≠ 1 rather than using (v i).IsNontrivial; likely definitionally/propositionally equivalent but not verified against the exact Mathlib definition.
